messages:
maya: FYI seeing a ~3x spike in preemptible evictions in us-west-2 this morning, a few streams got cut mid-response. Losing ~0.7% successful completions and tail latency is spiking. Thinking about a fallback: dual-path token streaming + micro-checkpoints. Thoughts?

ton y: ouch. timeline and repro? is this GCE preemptible churn or something else?

maya: evictions clustered 06:12-06:20 UTC. Rate ~1.5 evictions/min per node. GCE preemptible + a couple network flaps. Proxy logs show streaming connections reset with 502 upstream when worker drains.

infra-bot: K8S: PreemptNotice event for node gke-worker-44 at 2024-06-12T06:12:08Z (gracePeriod=30s)

oliver: can you paste a tiny example from the logs (headers/errors) so we can see where the cut happens?

maya: snippet:```
worker: RECEIVED_PREEMPT_NOTICE
proxy: stream cut, upstream reset 502
runtime: KV flush started, no persisted tokens
```

jia: Idea: on PREEMPT, write a micro-checkpoint of the last N generated tokens to redis (per request_id) and mark response as partial. The router on requeue tries redis first and replays tokens. Requires idempotent resume.

sam: tradeoffs: extra writes increase cost & a bit of latency. We should sample: only for requests >2s or token_count > 32.

tony: we already have prefix KV caching for prompts. Could reuse that keyspace to store a `resume_patch` (last 16 tokens + cursor). How to handle multi-requeues?

maya: proposal for best-effort flow: on PREEMPT: buffer last 16 tokens locally, attempt async write to redis with 100ms deadline. If write succeeds -> normal. If write fails -> attach buffered tokens to response metadata as `grace_tokens`. Router on new allocation: try redis, else fallback to `grace_tokens` embedded in request. This avoids blocking end-to-end latency.

oliver: router needs token-merge semantics. If we only have content, we can append until we reach a tokenizer boundary. Slightly messy but doable. Using token ids would be nicer but requires shared namespace.

jia: sample config:```
preempt_handling:
  checkpoint_tokens: 16
  async_write_deadline_ms: 100
  sample_only_for: total_duration_ms > 2000
  storage: redis://checkpoint/prefix
```

maya: load test summary: injected evictions at 10k req/min, long requests sample. Success rate for long requests improved from 98.3% -> 99.4%. Median latency +3ms, p99 +22ms on checkpointed requests.

sam: cost calc: avg checkpoint payload ~150 bytes. At 100M requests/month (sampled subset) this is ~15GB extra writes. Storage cost negligible but we should include request-level IOPS and egress.

tony: alternative is passive socket handoff: proxy keeps TCP open and proxies to new pod via stream-forwarding. Cross-node and cross-az makes this brittle and increases network hops. Not ideal.

maya: rollout plan: feature-flag gated. Canary 5% on preemptible-only pools first, then widen. Start off only for sampled long-running requests.

jia: telemetry/alerts to add: `preempt_checkpoint_write_success`, `stitch_success_rate`, `grace_tokens_used`, `extra_bytes_written_per_min`. Alert if checkpoint_write_success < 95% or stitch_success_rate < 90%.

oliver: one more thought: use a wear-leveling strategy on redis keys or TTLs to avoid hot keys on popular models. Also ensure checkpoints are encrypted if in customer-private flow.

sam: ok action items: maya + jia prototype worker-side buffer + async redis write + router stitch logic. tony adds canary routing rules + metrics. oliver to review merge semantics. I'll open a short-lived RFC and assign.

maya: I'll draft a tiny design doc + perf numbers and open PR soon. Will tag you all. :thumbsup:
